before-we-roll.plain: An opening letter on what this book is and is not: a field manual written from inside the festival scene, out of love for it, to help people spot those who exploit it.

the-cast.plain: The recurring people you will meet in the book's stories, all composites drawn from patterns seen across many festivals.

the-lexicon.plain: Twelve scene words explained before you start, from wook to PLUR, so newcomers can follow every chapter.

a-note-on-methodology.plain: Where the book's named tactics come from: clinical research on coercive control and manipulation, harm-reduction practice, and years of lived experience in the scene.

the-real-ones.plain: Before naming any manipulators, the book honours the people who keep festivals safe: harm-reduction volunteers, sanctuary crews and the friends who look out for others.

its-not-drama-its-warfare.plain: Chapter 1 explains why some festival conflict is not ordinary drama but deliberate manipulation, and introduces the main types of people who run it, from the openly predatory to the quietly embedded.

how-they-get-your-yes-before-you-finish-.plain: The twelve persuasion levers used on people at festivals, such as reciprocity, scarcity, social proof and fake authority, and how each one gets a yes before you have thought it through.

your-brain-on-day-three.plain: How sleep loss, heat, crowds and substances by the third day of a festival switch on predictable thinking errors, such as the halo effect and anchoring, that manipulators exploit.

your-body-made-a-friend-and-forgot-to-as.plain: The body chemistry of festival bonding, including oxytocin, dopamine and cortisol, and how it can create attachment to someone before you know who they are.

yes-is-a-sober-word.plain: Consent requires capacity. This chapter explains how intoxication affects the ability to consent and the tactics people use to take advantage of someone at their peak.

the-group-chat.plain: How some manipulators build trust in festival group chats weeks before the event, so that they already feel like a friend by the time you arrive.

the-weep-tent-hustle.plain: How emotional openness and healing spaces at festivals get exploited, through trauma dumping, claims of holding space, twin-flame talk and the healer who becomes a lover.

the-cult-that-calls-itself-family.plain: How festival camps can turn into controlling hierarchies, with camp-mom power grabs, wristband ranks, soft exile and group-chat pile-ons.

vendor-row-bloodsport.plain: How festival vendors and artists get exploited through booth fees, bad revenue splits, informal partnerships and payment runarounds.

the-love-of-it.plain: How the festival economy relies on people who would work for free, paying in tickets instead of wages and leaving workers uninsured.

the-bad-trip-babysitter.plain: How to help someone having a bad trip safely, and the manipulation that can happen around people in distress, with harm-reduction guidance from groups like the Zendo Project.
aka: how to help someone having a bad trip

the-tampon-bag.plain: How people are pressured or tricked into carrying drugs through festival gates for someone else, and the legal risk they take on.

the-road.plain: What to know on the way to a festival: traffic stops, searches and how information about you can leak from the people you travel with. Not legal advice.
aka: police stops on the way to festivals
your rights during a traffic stop

the-two-festivals.plain: Two people can attend the same festival and have very different weekends depending on gender, race, body and identity; this chapter covers why safety advice does not fit everyone.

the-batch.plain: Drug-checking and sourcing at festivals: why testing matters, how a bad batch spreads, and how the people who sell avoid responsibility.

the-free-one.plain: Why the free drink, pill or ride at a festival can come with an unspoken debt, and how that debt is collected later.

the-container.plain: How safe held space in ceremonies and workshops can become a sealed room where consent expires and doses go unmeasured.

the-undercover.plain: How to recognise a friendly stranger who keeps asking you to sell or source for them, and the patterns that suggest a setup.

the-rv.plain: What happens when a deal goes wrong or a camp gets robbed, and why some crimes at festivals leave victims with little recourse.

the-next-twelve-hours.plain: Written for the hours after a sexual assault at a festival: what is medically and practically available, how to preserve options, and where to get support.
aka: what to do after sexual assault

the-missing-friend.plain: What to do when a friend goes missing at a festival: the first hours, who to tell, and the details you need, starting with knowing their real name.

the-plug-wook.plain: How a drug supplier can build dependence and control, from free first doses to withdrawal threats.

the-lantern-family.plain: Inside a coercive festival crew: how a family frame, hierarchy and loyalty demands keep members from leaving.

the-festie-hollowing.plain: When festival life slowly replaces the rest of a person's life and identity, and the group uses that dependence as leverage.

the-re-entry-window.plain: The thirty-six hours after a festival when people are tired, emotional and easy to pressure, and the messages manipulators send in that window.

he-still-has-your-number.plain: When someone from a festival keeps contacting you afterward: how ongoing contact becomes stalking, and steps to protect yourself.

the-sober-set-captain.plain: A practical protocol for an anchor crew: a sober or low-dose captain, check-ins and a shared plan that keeps everyone safer.

the-long-comedown.plain: Recovering after a hard festival experience, including the 3 a.m. thoughts, memory gaps and re-entry into daily life.

have-you-been-the-wook.plain: An honest self-check for readers who may have crossed a line themselves: telling a pattern from a mistake, and making a real apology and amends.

the-authors-wook-confession.plain: The author names, in the first person, sixteen persuasion techniques this book itself used on the reader.

protecting-the-magic.plain: How a festival community builds its own immune system: whisper networks done responsibly, camp-lead duties and dealing with the missing stair.

what-to-tell-your-mom.plain: A chapter written to be handed to a parent or loved one: what festivals are actually like and how to talk about safety without fear.

the-tapers-reveal.plain: The book reveals the persuasion moves it used throughout, so readers can see how they work from the inside.

the-after-party.plain: The closing chapter: how to carry what you learned into a wook-proof life, with stronger friendships and a safer scene.

the-master-track-index.plain: Every named tactic in the book with its clinical name, the chapter it appears in and its primary counter-move.

the-recurring-cast.plain: Who the book's recurring characters are, where they appear and why they matter.

the-chemical-cage-mash-up.plain: What happens when several chemistry-driven tactics stack, and which chapters cover each combination.

the-safety-appendix-master.plain: All of the book's safety appendixes in one place, from substance safety to legal basics, for quick reference.

the-wook-proof-pre-event-checklist.plain: A printable checklist to run before every festival: crew plan, phone, money, medication, meeting points and exits.
aka: what to bring to a festival

the-full-counter-drop-master-list.plain: Every counter-move, called a counter-drop, from the book in one list, with the chapter it comes from.

the-wook-discog-complete.plain: A complete reference to the book's manipulator profiles, organised like a discography.

the-trifecta-diagnostic.plain: The book's central test: when three specific warning signs are present at once, treat the situation as manipulation.

the-capacity-spectrum.plain: A quick reference to what a person can and cannot consent to at each level of intoxication.

the-bystander-interruption-kit.plain: Three levels of bystander intervention anyone can use at a festival, with no expertise required.

the-anchor-system-and-bill-of-rights.plain: The full structure of the anchor crew system and a short bill of rights for everyone in a festival group.

festival-safety-and-harm-reduction-organ.plain: A list of festival safety and harm-reduction organisations, such as DanceSafe, the Zendo Project and the Fireside Project, to verify before you go.

the-good-samaritan-law-guide.plain: What Good Samaritan overdose laws are and how they can protect someone who calls for help, with a note that laws vary by state. Not legal advice.

the-long-exit-protocol.plain: A step-by-step protocol for leaving a high-control group safely and slowly.

the-timeline-of-recovery.plain: Realistic expectations for recovery after a festival trauma, week by week.

the-community-accountability-compact-tem.plain: A minimal template for a community accountability agreement a camp or crew can adopt.

the-sixteen-moves.plain: The sixteen persuasion moves the book used on its readers, listed by name.

the-five-sense-ground.plain: A five-senses grounding exercise for moments of panic or flashback.

the-wook-glossary.plain: An alphabetical field guide to every named tactic in the book, in scene language.

consent-and-capacity.plain: A one-page quick reference on consent and capacity, made to screenshot.

the-vocabulary-translation-list.plain: Common phrases used inside coercive groups translated into plain English.

the-financial-rights-of-scene-profession.plain: The short version of the financial rights artists, vendors and workers have in the festival industry.

the-institutional-betrayal-diagnostic.plain: A checklist to tell whether an organisation is failing or betraying its members when harm is reported.

the-immune-system-infrastructure-checkli.plain: An annual safety audit for camps and festivals: the structures that keep a community safe.

the-closing-argument.plain: The whole book in one page: why the magic is real, and how to protect it.
